c_connie.text: It looks at you the way ponies always do: long, grey and unimpressed. It has been in these fields since long before the roads.

c_connemarr.text: It looks at you the way ponies always do: long, grey and unimpressed. It has been in these fields since long before the roads.

turf_cutter.text: I cut the turf in May with a slean, a long narrow spade, and stack it to dry. By October it burns beautifully.
Peat's a thousand years in the making. A fire of it tells you stories. Mostly about rain.

kylemore_guide.text: Mitchell Henry built Kylemore for his wife Margaret, in 1867. She died young, in Egypt, and he built a little Gothic church beside the lake in her memory.
The Benedictine nuns have lived here since 1920. They make chocolate. I'm not trying to say that's the main reason for the visit.

pony_breeder.text: Connemara ponies are Ireland's best-known native breed. They're hardy, gentle, jump like deer and eat very little. They're a farmer's dream.
In August, Clifden holds the Connemara Pony Show. A champion can fetch more than a house. I've been offered a bicycle for mine.

wall_builder.text: I build the walls the old way: every stone fits, every gap breathes, no cement. A good wall lasts two hundred years.
The trick is to find the stone that wants to go there. It sounds mad. Try it. The wall tells you.

bens_walker.text: The Twelve Bens: twelve peaks, one view. On a bad day you see twelve fogs and one sheep.
Irish for Connemara is Conamara. It means 'the descendants of Conmac of the sea'. And yes, I could say all of it with a straight face, but a rainy day makes me silly.
